See ya out there!
Just announced! The Moccasin Bend Roll & Stroll is next Saturday, 9/26! 🎉 
 This event is organized by Chattanooga's Parks and Outdoors with Outdoor Chattanooga, with a ribbon-cutting at 10 Hamm Road (the NPS Gateway Site) and popsicles to be provided afterward at Renaissance Park. 
 Celebrate the addition of another 1.2-miles of greenway to the City's network, providing federal lands connectivity to the Moccasin Bend National Archaeological Site from nearby North Chattanooga. The project highlights the intersection of street safety and public space connections that stem from RPA's 2012 Moccasin Bend Gateway Plan, from the shared-use sidepath being added to the road diet it required along Manufacturers Road and Hamm Road, along with low impact development design strategies, and native plantings that frame the pathway. 
 Join neighbors, families, and outdoor enthusiasts to celebrate more than 10 years of partnerships toward the project between City Departments of Planning, Public Works, and Parks and Outdoors. The ribbon-cutting will be followed by a community trek down the brand-new, safely protected trail straight into Renaissance Park.

items.content_text:
CONGRATS TEAM!
 Hamilton County Breastfeeding Peer Counselors received the 2026 USDA Gold Award of Excellence for exemplary breastfeeding support and practices. The Tennessee Department of Health presented the award during its field staff training on August 27. Hamilton County’s program was one of only three in the state to receive this honor. To qualify, applicants must meet all 30 Gold Award criteria, demonstrating excellence in breastfeeding practices and support beyond the core components of the WIC Breastfeeding Model for Peer Counseling. Hamilton County’s peer counselors are Zina Difrancesco, Paula Allgood, Maricela Martinez, and Exelia Mejia Perez. They provide peer-to-peer education and support to expectant and postpartum mothers throughout their breastfeeding journeys. They are also available after hours to address concerns that may arise. Breastfeeding Coordinator Melissa Johnson, a registered nurse and certified lactation counselor, leads the team and provides specialized assistance to mothers facing a wide range of breastfeeding challenges.

Women working full time across OECD countries still earn, on average, only 90 cents for every dollar or euro earned by men, reflecting a gender wage gap of around 10%. 
 At the current pace of change, achieving equal pay could still take decades. 
 Pay transparency tools have emerged as a promising approach for addressing gender pay gaps by helping to identify pay disparities and support fairer pay practices.

 Destiny Washington is the founder and executive director of The Gold Horizon, an educational consulting agency dedicated to bridging the cap between research and actual implementation. items.content_text:
Chattajack Volunteers Needed :) —Help Bring Chattajack Village to Life!
 The vision for our new finish experience at River Gorge Ranch began nearly two years ago. Now, after months of planning and preparation, we need an incredible volunteer crew to help bring it to life on race day!
 So far, 26 volunteers have stepped forward to support our finish operations—19 at River Gorge Ranch and seven at the OC-6 takeout. We are extremely grateful for every one of them, but we still have 25 volunteer positions available at River Gorge Ranch.
 This will be an exciting and rewarding place to volunteer. You’ll be part of the inaugural Chattajack Village crew, first to welcome racers after their 31-mile journey through the Tennessee River Gorge and helping create the organized, encouraging and memorable experience they deserve.
 Volunteers will help set up and break down tents, organize resources, distribute finisher medals and nutrition, direct racers and their vessels, assist with shuttle loading, and keep everything flowing smoothly throughout the afternoon.
 There are roles for a variety of abilities, including positions that do not require heavy lifting.
 Thank you to the awesome folks who have already signed up as medical volunteers—you are critical to this event! We would love to add a few more, so if you possess medical training, please consider joining Amy Campbell’s amazing medical team. Opportunities are available aboard support boats and at the River Gorge Ranch takeout.
 This is the first year for Chattajack Village, and our volunteers will forever be the crew that helped launch it. We cannot do it without you!
 There's also always that nice CJ vol perk of: anyone who fulfills a Chattajack volunteer role in 2026 receives priority registration for the 2027 race.
 Come share the excitement, support our paddlers and help us create an unforgettable Chattajack experience!
 Sign up here:
 https://www.signupgenius.com/…/4090F48A4AD2EA7F58-65038929-…

items.content_text:
'Ten years ago, the EMC was an experiment. Today, it is a global community of urban leaders united by a shared commitment to making cities more equitable, sustainable and effective.'
 
This weekend, alumni, participants, faculty and invited urban practitioners return to LSE to mark ten years of the EMC and explore the urban questions that shape the programme today and in the future.
 
From the outset, the EMC was an experiment in bringing different forms of urban knowledge and practice into the same learning environment. The people working most directly with cities needed a learning environment equal to the scale and complexity of urban change. Their work cut across public policy, design, development, research, civic life and governance. The programme brought them together to examine the social, spatial, political, environmental and economic forces shaping urban life.
 
That remains the distinctive proposition of the EMC today: a degree that connects professional experience with critical urban research and allows participants to test ideas against the realities of other cities and forms of practice.
 
At this weekend’s Anniversary Forum, we will discuss themes that have been central to the EMC since its launch, including social inclusion, the urban environment, economic development and governance. The occasion brings the community back into conversation around the pressures now facing cities and the ways urban practice is changing in response.
 
The next decade of urban leadership will be shaped by climate risk, housing affordability, technological change, democratic pressure, fiscal constraint and new forms of institutional innovation.
 
Responding to those pressures will require city leaders and urban practitioners with the skills, judgement and perspective to work across disciplines, sectors and places, and make better decisions for cities. By connecting professional experience from across the globe with teaching grounded in critical urban research, the EMC today remains more relevant than ever.
 
Read more about how the EMC took shape and has developed here: https://lnkd.in/efgi4p64

#EMC10 #urbanpolicy

items.content_text:
The Tri-State Mutual Aid Association will host a two-day swiftwater rescue training event, bringing together regional emergency response teams to refine critical water rescue skills and enhance multi-agency coordination.
 The exercise on September 29-30, 2026 will take place on the Ocoee River. Hamilton County Special Tactics & Rescue Services (STARS), the Chattanooga Fire Department, and the Cleveland Fire Department are involved, in conjunction with Ocoee River State Park, TVA, and the US Forest Service. 
 Training evolutions will run throughout both days. Participating swiftwater rescue personnel will rotate through multiple high-intensity hands-on skills stations. 
 Training together on the water ensures swiftwater teams speak the same operational language, align safety protocols, and build the seamless trust required when combining forces during critical rescue operations. The Chattanooga Fire Fighters Association Local 820, Big Woody’s Tree Service, and Morning Pointe Senior Living have been strong supporters of this fantastic learning opportunity and we appreciate their partnership.

Critical services for survivors are at risk.
 Join advocates nationwide TODAY in urging Senate leadership to pass the bipartisan Crime Victims Fund Stabilization Act.
 The Crime Victims Fund supports services for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, child sexual abuse, trafficking, and other crimes. It is funded by monetary penalties from federal criminal cases, not taxpayer dollars. 
 But annual deposits have dropped by an average of $1.5 billion over the past decade, and the fund’s remaining buffer is gone. Programs are already reducing services, laying off staff, and closing their doors.
 The Stabilization Act would redirect unobligated funds from the False Claims Act into the CVF, helping preserve critical services without using taxpayer dollars.
 The House passed the bill unanimously. Now the Senate must act.
 Contact your U.S. senators TODAY. Survivors can’t afford to wait.
 #cvsa #LeaderJohnThune #SenSchumer #ChuckGrassley #SenatorDurbin #MarshaBlackburn #billhaggerty

In 2024, bilateral donors and EU institutions mobilised USD 23.4 billion in private finance (commercial money channelled towards sustainable development objectives).
 But how was that money mobilised, and where was it invested?
 The 2026 #OECD Development Co-operation Profiles highlight how providers of development assistance are using public resources to attract private investment and which sectors are receiving support.
 Insights include how:
 ➡️ The United States mobilised USD 6.9 billion, followed by EU institutions (USD 6 billion) and Germany (USD 2.5 billion)
 ➡️ The banking and financial services sector accounted for more than one-third of all mobilised private finance
 ➡️ The energy sector represented 23% of the total
 ➡️ Together, banking and financial services and energy attracted more than half of all mobilised private finance in 2024.
 Find out more in the #DCprofiles2026: https://brnw.ch/21x5VkK
 #OECDdevelopment

Today, we witnessed another decision being made without the community.
 Keeping the people of Lookout Valley in the dark about a decision that directly impacts their community is exactly why so many people are losing, or have already lost faith in elected officials and government.
 No communication. No transparency. No meaningful community engagement.
 Once again, residents are being asked to live with the consequences of decisions they were never given a meaningful opportunity to discuss.
 This is not how government should work!
 Whether you agree or disagree with the decision, the people affected deserve to know what is being considered. They deserve the opportunity to ask questions, receive honest answers, and have a seat at the table before decisions are made, not after everything has already been decided.
 As a County Commissioner, I believe transparency and community engagement are not favors we extend to residents. Those are responsibilities that come with public service.
 We cannot ask people to trust government while shutting them out of the process. Trust is built through transparency, accountability, and respect.
 The people of Lookout Valley deserved better communication. They deserved transparency. They deserved to be heard.
 I will continue to stand with communities across Hamilton County and insist on one simple principle:
 Nothing about a community should be decided without the community.

 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a shooting in the 200 block of Timber Knoll Drive.
 Shortly after 3:00 a.m. Wednesday, officers responded to the area after receiving reports of a person shot. Upon arrival officers located a 35-year-old man with a suspected non-life threatening gunshot wound. Hamilton County EMS transported the victim to the hospital, and CPD's Homicide and Crime Scene Units responded to investigate and process the scene.
 Preliminary findings indicate the suspect broke into the victim's vehicle and shot him when confronted. Investigators are currently pursuing all leads. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. 
 #CPDnews

A major milestone for one of Chattanooga’s most significant historic landscapes.
 Preserve Chattanooga joins National Park Partners and our community in celebrating the announcement that the Moccasin Bend Mental Health Institute will be relocated from Moccasin Bend.
 For decades, community advocates, preservationists, Indigenous partners, elected officials, and countless supporters have worked toward a shared vision for protecting this extraordinary place. Moccasin Bend preserves thousands of years of human history and represents a cultural landscape of local, regional, and national significance.
 Today’s announcement represents an important step toward protecting that history and realizing the long-held vision for Moccasin Bend as a fully interpreted part of Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park.
 We congratulate National Park Partners and everyone whose persistence and stewardship helped bring Chattanooga to this moment.
 Read National Park Partners’ full statement below.

The HCSO K-9 Unit is happy to support the LIFE FORCE Air Medical partnership with Puckett EMS as the first ground EMS service to provide dedicated emergency care and transport for K-9s, our valued partners.
 These efforts are essential to enabling emergency personnel to respond quickly and effectively if a K-9 is injured in the line of duty.
Puckett EMS, a member of the Priority Ambulance family of companies, has become the first ground ambulance service in Tennessee trained to provide dedicated transport for injured working K-9s and other working rescue dogs.
 During specialized training on Sept. 22, Puckett EMS providers learned how to recognize canine medical distress, safely handle and secure an injured working dog, provide emergency stabilization within applicable protocols and coordinate transport with handlers and receiving veterinary facilities.
 The training strengthens Puckett EMS’ support for the law enforcement officers, first responders and working K-9s who serve our communities every day.

items.title: A broken thermometer at a Chattanooga school resulted in a hazmat response and multiple people being transported to the...
items.content_text:
A broken thermometer at a Chattanooga school resulted in a hazmat response and multiple people being transported to the hospital Wednesday morning. On 9/23/26, Blue Shift companies responded to Dalewood Middle School at 1300 Shallowford Road after students and teachers were possibly exposed to mercury. 
 A thermometer was dropped during a routine experiment in a science lab. At first, it was suspected of containing mercury. It has now been determined that the thermometer was alcohol based and there was no harm to students or staff. 
 Officials treated the incident as a possible mercury exposure until the substance could be identified by an environmental company. 
 Fourteen students were transported by ambulance or personal vehicle to the hospital. Two teachers were also transported. They were taken to the hospital as a precautionary measure.
 The heating and air conditioning was shut down to the building and the rest of the student body was dismissed.
 Marion Environmental responded to the school to handle the remediation and confirmed that it was an alcohol thermometer. No mercury was involved. 
 CFD Hazmat 1, Special Operations, Squad 1, Engine 15, and members of the command staff responded to Dalewood Middle, in addition to CPD, Hamilton County EMS and officials with Hamilton County Schools.

A strong region is built when communities have the resources, partnerships and capacity to move forward together.

Today, we’re proud to share the Southeast Tennessee Development District 2026 Annual Report, reflecting a year of meaningful investment and collaboration across the communities we serve.

This year, SETD helped secure $51.9 million in grant funding for local governments, managed more than $450 million in community projects, connected thousands of older adults and individuals with disabilities with critical resources, and provided 13,433 workforce services to 721 regional employers.

But the story of this year is bigger than any one number.

It can be seen in infrastructure moving from plans to reality, new investments reaching our communities, people gaining skills and pathways to employment, older adults remaining connected and independent, and local leaders working across community lines to address shared priorities.

That is the role SETD is proud to play: bringing people, resources and expertise together to help Southeast Tennessee turn shared goals into progress.

None of this work happens alone. We are grateful to our local governments, board members, funding partners, community organizations and regional partners who continue to trust us and work alongside us.

Building Together for a Thriving Southeast Tennessee.

Commission Meeting Summary — September 21, 2026
 Airport Advisory Board: The commission approved Resolution 583, formally appointing Jack Farrow, John Record, Heath Merz, Michael Brown, and Zoe Krohne to the Airport Advisory Board.
 Airport Retaining Wall: The commission approved a $55,000 task order with Ardurra Group (parent company of Cannon & Cannon) to design repairs for the failing retaining wall behind the Airport Terminal, funded through the enterprise fund. Commissioners discussed drainage concerns, road conditions, and financing options, and agreed to get a rough budget after preliminary design before finalizing how the project will be paid for.
 Also approved: FY27 Airport Maintenance Grant Contract and the August Finance Report.
 City Manager's Report:
 - The city will take over direct management of the library, ending its contract with the outside provider, and will coordinate with the state regional library system for ordinance updates & guidance.
 - Imagination Station: Cannon & Cannon is developing proposals; a public open house is being proposed so residents can review and ask questions.
 - Iron Rail Cams will propose live-view cameras at the Thatcher Switch/Tucker Road railroad crossing — at no cost to the city.
 - A new commissioner orientation book is in the works, along with Sunshine Law training for city boards.
 Commissioner Remarks:
 - The city's audit is underway, with a first draft expected around October.
 - A citizen-suggested idea for a library food pantry will be discussed at an upcoming workshop.
 - Christmas Parade Survey results will be presented at the commission workshop on Monday, September 28th.
 Watch the full meeting recording here: https://www.collegedaletn.gov/…/agenda…/livestream/index.php

Commissioners discussed drainage concerns, road conditions, and financing options, and agreed to get a rough budget after preliminary design before finalizing how the project will be paid for.
Also approved: FY27 Airport Maintenance Grant Contract and the August Finance Report.
City Manager's Report:
- The city will take over direct management of the library, ending its contract with the outside provider, and will coordinate with the state regional library system for ordinance updates & guidance.
- Imagination Station: Cannon & Cannon is developing proposals; a public open house is being proposed so residents can review and ask questions.
- Iron Rail Cams will propose live-view cameras at the Thatcher Switch/Tucker Road railroad crossing — at no cost to the city.
- A new commissioner orientation book is in the works, along with Sunshine Law training for city boards.
Commissioner Remarks:
- The city's audit is underway, with a first draft expected around October.
- A citizen-suggested idea for a library food pantry will be discussed at an upcoming workshop.
- Christmas Parade Survey results will be presented at the commission workshop on Monday, September 28th.
Watch the full meeting recording here: https://www.collegedaletn.gov/…/agenda…/livestream/index.php

items.content_text:
Starting the semester strong is ideal for any student, but many quickly learn that old study habits, time management methods and organizational skills don’t work efficiently. UTC offers many resources to guide students in the right direction to achieve the strongest growth possible. UTC’s Center for Academic Support and Advisement (CASA) is a resource all students can turn to when this shift becomes difficult. 👏 
 CASA supports students through tutoring, supplemental instruction and peer-led academic coaching. These free services emphasize becoming independent, active learners. 
 CASA is located in UTC Library Room 335 and is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Walk-ins are welcome, and students can schedule appointments through MyMocsNet. 
 🔗  Learn more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/learning-to-adapt-how-casa-helps-st…/
